### GPU backend artifact policy

GPU support follows a host/device split, not whole-program GPU execution:
ordinary Python control flow and runtime semantics stay on the selected CPU
backend (`llvm` or `self`), while explicitly annotated GPU kernels may lower to
a device backend such as Metal.

Metal artifact staging is now:

1. Default executable packaging: embed the `.metallib` bytes in the host
   Mach-O executable and load them through Metal's data-library API.
2. Debug/fallback packaging: still emit a sidecar `.metallib` next to the host
   executable so generated Metal source/AIR/library artifacts remain inspectable
   and the runtime can fall back if an executable lacks the embedded section.

Do not claim that `--gpu-backend=metal` makes the whole Python program run on
the GPU. MLX support is a planned first-class target, but the current state is
not yet MLX-native-capable: supporting a Metal device backend creates useful
substrate for MLX-like execution, while actual Apple `mlx` support remains a
separate package/C-extension/runtime integration and array-runtime milestone. A
valid MLX claim must prove that pcc1 can import/run the package in a
mode-labeled CPython-compat/proxy path, or that an explicitly scoped pcc-native
MLX-compatible array runtime exists. Metal kernel compilation alone is not an
MLX support claim.

NumPy and MLX are foundation layers for later accelerator-package support, but
they do not make vLLM or TileLang supported by themselves. Treat vLLM and
TileLang as sibling package/ecosystem targets, not as dependencies of each
other. Each target is layered on:

1. generic package install/inspect/linkage metadata, with no `if package ==
   "vllm"` or `if package == "tilelang"` compiler/runtime special case;
2. CPython C-extension ABI and Python proxy interop inherited from the NumPy
   path, including honest `--python-libpython=off` rejection at the first
   incompatible installed extension boundary;
3. tensor/array/runtime interop learned from NumPy/MLX and package-specific
   compiler/runtime surfaces, with mode-labeled ownership, conversion, and
   dispatch boundaries;
4. platform accelerator support: CUDA/PyTorch-style extension stacks for vLLM
   and TVM/kernel-DSL compiler stacks for TileLang are not proven by Apple
   Metal work, while MLX/Metal work is the Apple GPU substrate. Cross-backend
   claims must name the backend and package mode.

Track vLLM and TileLang as sibling platform routes, not one generic package.
The numbering below is route enumeration only; it is not a dependency order:

1. Standard vLLM route: PyTorch plus CUDA/ROCm/XPU native extension kernels,
   Hugging Face/model-format packages (`transformers`, `tokenizers`,
   `safetensors`, `sentencepiece`), serving/runtime packages (`fastapi`,
   async/event-loop, metrics, IPC), and their build/link surfaces. This route
   is not proved by Metal or MLX work.
2. macOS Apple Silicon route: `vllm-metal` on top of MLX/MLX-LM/MLX-VLM and
   Metal-capable Apple GPU runtime behavior. This is the route to prioritize on
   a Mac, but it is still a CPython-extension/package-runtime integration
   target until pcc-native tensor/runtime support exists.
3. TileLang route: `tilelang` as a Pythonic tile-level GPU/CPU kernel DSL and
   compiler stack on TVM/FFI, NumPy, Torch, Z3, scikit-build/Cython/C++, and
   backend-specific device code paths such as CUDA/HIP/Metal. It is same-level
   package/ecosystem work alongside vLLM, not a vLLM downstream target.
4. MiniMind Apple Silicon validation route: `jingyaogong/minimind` is a real
   pcc1 training/inference validation target for the Apple Silicon arm64 issue
   request, not a downstream of vLLM or TileLang. It exercises PyTorch,
   Transformers/tokenizers, datasets, model checkpoint loading, training loops,
   and device selection (`cpu`, `mps`, future `metal`/MLX paths) as a
   mode-labeled package/runtime gate.
5. Multi-Mac distributed route: pcc distributed training and serving is a
   sibling runtime/compiler target, not a vLLM-only feature and not a TileLang
   downstream. It covers `PCCDistSession`/world/mesh identity, control-plane
   admission, transport backends (`tcp-ring`, future `quic`, future
   `jaccl-rdma`), collective APIs, FSDP-like sharding, KV block lifecycle, and
   measurement/skip taxonomy for single-process, local-process, localhost, and
   real multi-Mac modes.

TVM/TIRx and TileLang-native work is a separate kernel-lowering route, not a
package-import claim. The source research note is
`tmp_research/deep-research-tvm.md`. When implementing this route, use the
local Metal-enabled TileLang source under `~/tilelang`
(`/Users/jiamo/tilelang`) as the first
code reference, especially its backend registries, host/device split, Metal
pipeline, Metal host-context hook, and Metal GEMM benchmark. Clone upstream TVM
only when a selected implementation or investigation slice needs current TVM
source that is not already present in `~/tilelang`; clone it outside
the pcc repo under `~/pcc_refs/` and record the exact revision. A TVM
clone or local TileLang reference is research evidence only, not pcc support.
If TVM C++ is translated or extracted, it must follow the successful pcc LLVM
pattern: translate only a verifiable, bounded reference/oracle subset such as
TIR object shapes, pass/golden-output behavior, target split, and Metal
lowering reference. Do not make a full TVM C++ runtime/object system,
PackedFunc/FFI, registry, or build stack rewrite a prerequisite for pcc GPU
support. The implementation root remains pcc's own Kernel IR / TIRx / Metal
path; TVM-derived code is oracle/reference material unless a focused pcc gate
proves otherwise.

LLVM infrastructure reference impact for GPU/TIRx/Metal: internalize the LLVM
architecture lesson, do not keep the PDF as a runtime reference and do not make
LLVM the GPU owner. The durable LLVM reference source lives under
`~/pcc_refs/llvm-project-20.1.8-full-depth1`, while upstream TVM lives under
`~/pcc_refs/apache-tvm-full-depth1` and the local TileLang implementation under
`~/tilelang` (`/Users/jiamo/tilelang`). The lesson for pcc is LLVM-style
modularity: stable IR,
explicit data layout/address spaces, TargetMachine/capability separation,
verifier-first pass boundaries, and artifact phases that make IR, source,
object/library, host launch, and runtime execution separate claims. GPU work
must apply those lessons to pcc's own Kernel IR / TIRx / Metal path.

A valid vLLM or TileLang claim must say exactly which mode is proven:
`package-inspect/install only`, `cpython-compat import/proxy`, `pcc-native
no-libpython boundary rejection`, or a future `pcc-native tensor/runtime`
implementation. Do not describe vLLM or TileLang as complete until a focused
package gate for that target and at least one real import or documented
platform-skip gate exists.

A valid MiniMind claim must additionally say which device path was exercised:
`cpu`, `torch-mps`, `mlx-metal`, `pcc-metal-kernel`, or `skipped-with-reason`.
Running MiniMind under pcc1 in CPython-compat/proxy mode proves only package
execution and boundary diagnostics unless the gate also proves a real Apple GPU
device path. Do not claim that pcc1 solves MiniMind Apple Silicon training or
inference until a focused pcc1 train and infer gate either runs on the target
device or records the exact external blocker.

A valid distributed-runtime claim must say exactly which execution mode is
proven: `design/reference routing only`, `single-process simulation`,
`local-process loopback`, `localhost tcp-ring`, `real multi-mac tcp-ring`,
`quic`, `jaccl-rdma`, or `skipped-with-reason`. It must also state the security
mode (`insecure-dev`, `tls`, `mtls`, or `signed-manifest-only`) and whether the
claim covers training collectives, serving/KV block movement, or only metadata.
Do not describe multi-Mac training, vLLM distributed serving, JACCL/RDMA, or
secure cluster admission as complete from a single-process oracle.

A valid TVM/TIRx or TileLang-native claim must instead say which compiler mode
is proven: `design/reference routing only`, `package-inspect/install only`,
`kernel-IR golden only`, `host/device split IR only`, `Metal source/metallib
artifact only`, `host launch runtime`, or future `pcc-native tensor/runtime`.
Do not describe this route as complete until explicit kernel functions lower
through a mode-labeled host/device split and at least one focused kernel gate
runs or skips with a documented platform/toolchain reason.

## Document index and working protocol (do not delete)

This file is the long-form goal and work protocol. It is not a warehouse for
every branch plan, issue, investigation, or historical ledger.

### Reference-document policy

Reference documents are routed, not absorbed. This prompt is an index and work
protocol, not a warehouse for every plan, issue, investigation, or historical
ledger.

Keep this file focused on the global objective, priority model, P0 parity
policy, coverage ratchet, claim hygiene, validation gates, and output contract.
Put branch-specific references in `docs/current-goal-state.md` unless the
reference is itself a global protocol authority, a global completion authority,
or part of the required startup set.

The route map in `docs/current-goal-state.md` is intentionally trigger-based:

| Tier | Default read? | Owner | Rule |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Startup authorities | yes | `AGENTS.md`, this file, `docs/current-goal-state.md` | Read exactly the required startup set before selecting or resuming work. |
| Completion authorities | on claim | JSON baselines and focused tests | Use current gates or baselines as proof; prose is not enough. |
| Active-branch routes | on boundary | `docs/current-goal-state.md` | Open only the row triggered by the selected slice or failing gate. |
| Deferred branch routes | no | `docs/current-goal-state.md` | Do not open unless the selected task leaves the active branch or a failure crosses that boundary. |
| Historical ledgers | no | `todo.md` if present | Use only for context, never as completion proof without current tests. Removed ledgers must not be treated as required startup material. |

When adding a reference, first decide whether it changes startup behavior,
claim authority, or a branch-specific decision boundary. If it does not, do not
add it. If it does, add it to `docs/current-goal-state.md` unless it belongs to
the global protocol surface of this file.

Agent-written documentation must be English unless preserving direct user
text, an existing section title, a historical quote, or a test/output literal.

### Reference ownership rules

- `codex-goal-prompt.md` owns global rules and should not grow branch-plan
  bodies.
- `docs/current-goal-state.md` owns the active audit and branch-specific
  reference routing.
- `docs/investigations/INDEX.md` is the only default entry point into
  investigation documents. Keep it routeable by failure shape; do not make the
  whole `docs/investigations/` directory startup material.
- JSON baselines and current test results own completion claims.
- Historical ledgers explain context only; they do not prove current success.
- If a referenced document has no clear trigger for when an agent should open
  it, do not add that reference yet.

### Investigation routing rule

For non-trivial pcc1/self-host, runtime, bootstrap, GC, backend, package, or
project failures, open `docs/investigations/INDEX.md` first and then exactly the
matching investigation file. If the index cannot route the failure by symptom,
subsystem, or known gate, update the index or create a focused investigation
entry instead of copying investigation content into this prompt.

### Authority split

| Document | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Repository operating rules: timeouts, temp-file discipline, destructive-command policy, validation expectations, and bootstrap definition of done. | Goal selection, evidence promotion, or branch-specific routing. |
| `codex-goal-prompt.md` | North-star objective, priority model, active task board, P0 parity policy, coverage ratchet, pcc1/pcc2 difference classification, gates, claim hygiene, output contract, and links to current/archive evidence. | Detailed branch plans, issue bodies, investigation bodies, or historical ledger content copied from elsewhere. |
| `docs/current-goal-state.md` | Short selected-task audit, latest evidence, weak boundaries, claim authorities, and on-demand reference routing. | Replacement of this long-form goal/protocol. |

### Required startup set

Read exactly these files first, in order:

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `codex-goal-prompt.md`
3. `docs/current-goal-state.md`

No branch plan, issue file, investigation, performance plan, GC reference,
NumPy plan, package/ecosystem plan, or historical ledger is part of startup by
default. Open additional documents only when the selected task, a failing gate,
or a claim boundary crosses into the routed branch in
`docs/current-goal-state.md`.

### Goal-mode execution authorization

When this prompt is running under `/goal` continuation, the current selected
task, blocker, gates, and routed debug/investigation steps named by
`AGENTS.md`, this file, or `docs/current-goal-state.md` are the user's active
work request. Non-destructive commands directly required by that route are
authorized: focused gates, focused builds, focused reproducers, source search,
routed investigation reads, diagnostics, and reruns of the same focused gate
after a fix.

Do not stop for separate permission merely because the required next step is a
test, gate, build, focused repro, source search, investigation read, or
diagnostic command. If a required gate fails, continue into the documented
debug/investigation route instead of stopping.

This authorization does not override repository safety rules: every shell
command still needs an explicit timeout; destructive git/filesystem operations
remain prohibited unless explicitly requested; external services, production
state, credentials, paid resources, and real user data still require explicit
permission; and a focused gate must not be broadened into unrelated expensive
or full-suite validation unless the current docs require it.

Before continuing past a meaningful state change, apply the state-sync hard
stop in §0: update `docs/current-goal-state.md` while the evidence is fresh.
The document must name the current failure shape, last commands/results,
confirmed/denied hypotheses, and the next gate. Running more diagnostics or
editing more code while the state file still advertises stale evidence is a
protocol violation.

### Green-gate local commit workflow

When user-authorized goal work completes a substantial fix or feature and the
required bootstrap/fallback/GC gates for that claim have passed, make one local
git commit for that completed work unless the current user explicitly says not
to commit. Do not push.

The commit title must name the behavioral fix or feature. The commit body must
summarize the code changes, tests/gates run, and any remaining claim boundary.
Do not commit before the required gates finish; do not include unrelated dirty
work; do not use destructive git commands to manufacture a clean tree.

Ignored files are not automatically part of the commitable worktree, even when
they are relevant to the current discussion. Never use `git add -f` or any
other force-add mechanism for an ignored file unless the user explicitly names
that exact ignored path and says to force-add it. If a requested documentation
edit lands in an ignored local-state file such as `codex-goal-prompt.md`, leave
it uncommitted and report that boundary instead of overriding `.gitignore`.

Do not mark the goal `blocked` because a current gate, repro, or debug step
needs to run. `blocked` is only valid for a real external impasse after the
repeated-blocker audit in the active `/goal` context is satisfied.

### Reference routing contract

- If prose conflicts with an authoritative JSON baseline or current test
  result, the baseline or test result wins.
- On resume, completion is determined by the current task/status rows plus
  rerunning the named gates. Historical archive rows are context only and must
  not be used as proof that a task is currently complete.
- Treat routed documents as on-demand pointers, not mandatory startup reads.
- Add or change branch-specific references in `docs/current-goal-state.md`,
  not in this file.
- Add references here only when they are global protocol authorities, global
  completion authorities, or required by the startup set itself.
- Do not move full content from other docs into this file. Add indexes,
  evidence summaries, and references only.
- New agent-written documentation must be in English unless preserving a
  direct quote, historical note, user text, or existing section title.

### Edit rules

- Do not change the north-star objective or shrink the active goal to the
  current slice.
- Do not delete the P0 parity blocker policy, coverage ratchet, pcc1/pcc2
  difference classification, testing gates, claim hygiene, evidence routing, or
  output format.
- A long ledger may be messy, but evidence must not be lost in the name of
  cleanup. Move old evidence to an archive/reference file instead of deleting
  it.
- Keep current status synchronized in `0.1`, `0.3`, `0.4`, and
  `docs/current-goal-state.md`. Keep `0.5` as an archive pointer only; do not
  paste historical ledger rows back into this prompt.
- For `S-P0-SELF`, unsupported Python syntax/runtime semantics must be fixed
  for real and ratcheted through pcc1/pcc2 coverage. Do not rewrite or bypass
  constructs to fake completion.

```text
latest_gc_barrier_py_list_reverse_update: 2026-07-05 — addressed one exact barrier omission from `AUD-P0-GC-BARRIER-WRITE-AUDIT`. `py_list_reverse` swapped the published `l->items[i]` / `l->items[j]` slots with raw writes even though list item slots are GC-tracked owner slots and backend #3/#4 require load/store barriers. The C runtime now loads both sides with `pcc_gc_load_ptr`, temporarily retains the two borrowed items across the two stores, writes the slots through `pcc_gc_store_ptr(lst, &l->items[i/j], ...)`, then releases the temporaries. The pcc-Python mirror now uses the same retain + `pcc_gc_store_ptr(lst, ptr_add(items, ...), ...)` shape. Source guards first failed on the missing C and pcc-Python reverse barriers, then passed; the follow-on retain-order guard locks the no-premature-release swap ordering. latest_gc_slot_direct_valueclass_payload_roots_update: 2026-07-05 — direct `@pcc.valueclass` payload locals and parameters now register every pointer-bearing payload field as its own borrowed GC frame slot. The registration uses the real field address inside the payload alloca, so backend #4 root rewriting heals the payload field itself; nested valueclass payload fields are discovered recursively. The entry-block setup now inserts each field GEP after the payload alloca instead of poisoning the alloca insertion cache, avoiding same-block use-before-def IR. Ownership classification now treats direct valueclass payload attribute loads as borrowed, so `b.items.append(...)` no longer emits `pcc_gc_release(b.items)` for a field still stored inside the payload. New regression `tests/python/gc_production_contract/test_valueclass_direct_payload_roots.py` first failed on all five backends (#0/#4 BAD_INCREF; #1/#2/#3 lost list payload), then passed; follow-up coverage now also keeps `Holder(Nested(list, str), list, str)` in direct payload form and checks local, function-parameter, method-receiver, typed function-return, constructor-temporary, walrus-target, and reassignment-target nested pointer fields across explicit collections, including `touch_holder(Holder(...))`, `Holder(...).touch_holder()`, `if (walrus := Holder(...))` readback after collection, and overwriting a payload local after collection before typed-callee mutation/readback. Gates: focused direct/nested/constructor-temporary/walrus/reassignment payload 5-GC contract -> 5 passed; boxed valuebox + existing valueclass pointer payload contracts -> 10 passed; valueclass runtime/source-shape/unboxed batch -> 103 passed; fallback/no-libpython baselines -> 18 passed; full `tests/python/gc_production_contract` -> 140 passed; touched-file `py_compile` passed. `tests/python/test_bootstrap_gate_baseline.py` was run but skipped 4 tests because its canonical bootstrap artifact paths are absent; no bootstrap or pcc1 fixed-point claim is made. latest_gc_slot_cext_dynamic_tag_dispatch_update: 2026-07-04 — dynamic pcc-native C-extension type tags are now excluded from pcc instance/valuebox layout dispatch in both C and pcc-Python runtime tiers. C backend0 cycle collection skips C-extension tags in `py_gc_maybe_finalize_unreachable` and calls `pcc_capi_dealloc_cext_object(...)` before the user-instance fallback in `py_gc_dealloc_unreachable`; C tracing backends do the same in PASS 0 / PASS 2, and `py_user_del_dispatch` itself now refuses C-extension tags before reading `PyInstanceObject` fields. The pcc-Python mirrors add the same `pcc_capi_is_cext_type_tag(...)` / `pcc_capi_dealloc_cext_object(...)` boundaries in `py_obj_gc.py`, `py_gc_backend.py`, `py_obj_dealloc.py`, and `py_dunder.py`; backend-4 pcc-Python relocation support also rejects opaque C-extension tags in both supported-tag and payload-copy paths. Gates: new behavior probe proves a dynamic managed C-extension object survives `py_user_del_dispatch` without `PY_FLAG_FINALIZED` and then `Py_DECREF` calls the managed C-API dealloc path; source guard locks C and pcc-Python finalizer/dealloc/slot/relocation dispatch ordering; touched-file `py_compile` passed; `tests/python/test_gc_update_referents.py` -> 20 passed; existing managed-dealloc C-extension gate -> 1 passed; extension module-state roots -> 5 passed; C runtime archive rebuild passed with pre-existing warnings; pcc-Python runtime archive rebuild passed with pre-existing warnings. `bootstrap: not run; focused dynamic C-extension tag dispatch/mirror slice only, no pcc1 fixed-point or full 5-GC production-complete claim.`
latest_gc_slot_py_obj_gc_cext_instance_update: 2026-07-04 — the pcc-Python backend0 cycle-collector mirror now excludes dynamic C-extension tags before its instance/valuebox/user-class slot helper. `_py_obj_gc_visit_instance_owner_slots(...)` checks `pcc_capi_is_cext_type_tag(tag) != 0` before the `tag != 11 and tag != 200 and tag < 104` fallback, matching the C-tier rule that opaque pcc-native C-extension objects are not pcc `PyInstanceObject` / `PyValueBoxObject` layouts. latest_gc_slot_py_cext_object_mirror_update: 2026-07-04 — the pcc-Python GC mirrors now route dynamic pcc-native C-extension object slots through the same object-family bridge as the C runtime instead of only excluding those tags from instance/valuebox layouts. A new C ABI shim `pcc_capi_visit_cext_object_slots_i64(...)` adapts the C `PyObjSlotVisitor` `int32_t role` to pcc-Python's current i64 function-parameter ABI, then `py_gc_backend.py` and `py_obj_gc.py` pass local callback functions that hand `tp_traverse` / fake-header `Py_VISIT` lvalue slots to `_py_obj_visit_slot(...)` / `_py_obj_gc_visit_slot(...)` with offset 0. The bridge is called before the instance/valuebox helper in trace, subtract, promotion, backend-4 remap, clear, backend0 get_referents/mark, and backend0 clear paths; allocation failure for the temporary callback context aborts instead of silently skipping GC slots. Gates: new source-contract test first failed on the missing pcc-Python extern/helper, then passed; `tests/python/test_gc_update_referents.py` -> 21 passed; touched-file `py_compile` passed; default C runtime archive rebuild passed with pre-existing warnings; pcc-Python runtime archive rebuild passed with pre-existing warnings; `PCC_RUNTIME_CC=pcc PCC_RUNTIME_HIGH=py PCC_GC_BACKEND=0 tests/python/test_gc_g1_cycle_collector.py` -> 8 passed; adjacent generational pcc-Python slot-helper/source subset -> 8 passed after fixing a stale source-slice test; adjacent backend4 class metadata source guard -> 1 passed. latest_gc_slot_cext_trash_defer_update: 2026-07-04 — dynamic pcc-native C-extension type tags are now excluded before the generic `type_tag >= PY_TYPE_USER` trash/dealloc deferral catch-all. C `pcc_trash_should_defer(...)` and the split `pcc_dealloc_should_defer(...)` both check `pcc_capi_is_cext_type_tag(...)` before their switch/default logic, and the split helper now returns `1` for the explicit pointer-bearing cases instead of falling through to the default expression. The pcc-Python runtime mirror `_dealloc_should_defer(...)` uses the same dynamic-tag exclusion before its `tag >= 100` fallback. latest_gc_slot_cext_object_update: 2026-07-04 — pcc-native C-extension dynamic objects now form an explicit object-slot family in the C runtime. `py_obj_visit_slots` calls `pcc_capi_visit_cext_object_slots(...)` before the generic instance/valuebox walker; `pcc_capi_visit_cext_object_slots` invokes the extension type's `tp_traverse` through the fake-header `Py_VISIT` slot bridge and hands lvalue slots to `PyObjSlotVisitor` as owned slots. Dynamic C-API type tags are now excluded from `pcc_gc_visit_instance_owner_slots`, and backend-4 relocation-copy no longer treats opaque C-extension objects as ordinary pcc user instances. The libpython runtime variant has an explicit no-op stub because pcc-native extension tags do not exist there. latest_gc_slot_class_creation_payload_update: 2026-07-04 — backend-4 class metadata payload spans now cover initial class creation and method-table growth, not only relocation-copy. status: DONE_WEAK - The C runtime now exposes the named object-slot contract entrypoints: `PyObjSlotVisitor`, `PY_OBJ_SLOT_OWNED`, `PY_OBJ_SLOT_BORROWED_TRACED`, `PY_OBJ_SLOT_BORROWED_UPDATE_ONLY`, `py_obj_visit_slots(...)`, and `py_obj_update_slot(...)`. The public visitor delegates through the existing covered-family walkers and preserves the class metadata role split: method-table functions and `del_method` are update/promote-only, not mark roots. Backend-4 remap now heals object referents through `py_obj_update_slot`; C trace and pcc-Python trace/subtract consumers now load slots through the relocation barrier before graph traversal. Backend #0 cycle collection now consumes `py_obj_visit_slots` for visit/subtract/mark/get_referents and clear, instead of carrying a separate per-type graph walker, and the pcc-Python backend0 cycle-collector mirror now consumes equivalent local slot-role helpers for visit/subtract/get_referents/mark/clear plus local root-slot helpers for global/frame/continuation/scheduler runtime-root marking. Scalar/native-wrapper families with no object-inline PyObject slots are now explicitly classified in C and pcc-Python instead of falling through implicitly; thread wait queues remain external scheduler-rooted waiter nodes. Backend-4 now registers list/dict/set relocated external payload tables, continuation stack slot arrays, and initial plus relocated class bases/mro/methods arrays as owner payload spans on both C and pcc-Python sides; method-table `realloc` growth uses payload-span retargeting to preserve virtual zpage offsets when the base pointer moves. The pcc-Python runtime mirror now has helper coverage for list/tuple/dict/set owner slots, fixed owner slots, `PY_TYPE_CONTINUATION` stack slots, instance/valuebox class+field/dynamic-attrs slots, `PY_TYPE_CLASS` metadata roles, mapped roots, scheduler roots, no-pointer wrappers, moved list/dict/set external payload span registration, continuation stack payload-span registration, class creation/method-growth/relocation payload-span registration, backend0 cycle-collector get/mark/subtract/clear consumers, and backend0 runtime-root marking; the covered object helper families are consumed by trace, cycle-ref subtraction, generational promotion, backend-4 remap, and clear where applicable. latest_bytearray_extend_update: 2026-06-19 — follow-on `pproxy --test` reached HTTP 200 through the remote SOCKS server, then failed at `pproxy/server.py:881` with `AttributeError: extend` for `body = bytearray(); body.extend(s)`. Added generic no-libpython `py_bytearray_extend(o, iterable)` in the C runtime and pcc-Python runtime port, plus frontend statement lowering that rewrites bytearray lvalue `extend` to a new bytearray binding instead of unsafe in-place growth of the fixed inline buffer. Dynamic attribute `.extend` now runtime-dispatches bytearray/list/user-object cases without regressing user-defined or list `extend`. Focused red/green gates now passed: `tests/python/test_native_bytearray_empty_ctor.py` plus dynamic extend guards -> 6 passed; `make -B -C pcc/py_runtime libpy_runtime.a` passed with pre-existing warnings. Next gate remains rebuild canonical pcc1, verify no libpython, rerun `pcc1 -m pproxy --test`, then start the exact proxy command if the test path is clean.

Active investigation: `docs/investigations/pcc1-pproxy-gc4-live-proxy-readuntil-empty.md`. latest_pproxy_read_until_pop_update: 2026-06-19 — reductions showed the buffer/socket data was intact (`reader.read_until(...).result()` had the full header), so added generic stdlib `StreamReader.read_until(...)` to stabilize the pproxy-compatible method surface. Bypassing that await in a `/tmp` pproxy copy exposed the next pcc1-only issue: `list.pop(0)` on a dynamic receiver lowered to `py_dict_pop` and raised `KeyError`; host pcc already lowered it to `py_list_pop`. Added DynType `pop` list/dict/user runtime tag dispatch plus host and pcc1 smoke regressions. Host focused gates pass; pcc1 smoke remains red until the canonical pcc1 rebuild.
latest_pproxy_schedule_filter_update: 2026-06-19 — temporary-copy live instrumentation progressed to `schedule(rserver, salgorithm, host_name, port)` and reproduced `native function got too many positional arguments` at `next(filter(filter_cond, rserver), None)`. Minimized generic roots: (1) value-position `Name("filter")` fallback-matched `__nested_filter_cond` because hoisted nested-name resolution accepted any `__nested_filter_*` prefix; it now only accepts numeric collision suffixes. (2) after that fix, strict no-libpython exposed missing `next(filter(predicate, iterable), default)` support; `iterator_builtin_lowering.py` now emits a generic iterator/predicate loop. Focused host gates pass: touched-file `py_compile` and `tests/python/test_native_map_filter.py` -> 4 passed. Next gate: rebuild canonical `build/bootstrap-pytest-self/pcc1`, rerun pcc1 smoke including `test_pcc1_filter_lambda_method_next_default`, verify no-libpython linkage, then retry `pproxy --test` and the exact live proxy command.
```

### 0.2 Status vocabulary

Use only these status words. Do not invent vague alternatives.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DISCOVERED` | Found in docs or code, but not selected for the current turn. |
| `TODO_READY` | Clear enough to implement one minimal closed loop directly. |
| `TODO_NEEDS_DESIGN` | Needs design, investigation, or a minimal repro before implementation. |
| `CLAIM_RISK` | Docs or code may overclaim; add a gate or downgrade the claim. |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | Currently being implemented in this turn. |
| `BLOCKED` | Blocked by a concrete blocker; record the blocker, evidence, and next step. |
| `TESTING` | Implementation exists and focused / pcc1 / no-host / perf gates are running. |
| `DONE_WEAK` | Implementation or tests exist, but evidence is not strong enough for a broad claim. |
| `BACKEND_PARTIAL` | A runtime/GC-touching feature passes some but not all five GC backends (see the 5-GC Production Equality Rule in G-track). Not production-complete; name the passing/failing backends. |
| `DONE_STRONG` | Implementation, negative tests, regression tests, related gates, and evidence are all present. For a runtime/GC-touching feature, this REQUIRES the common GC production contract green under `PCC_GC_BACKEND=0..4` (5-GC Production Equality Rule). |
| `SKIPPED_WITH_REASON` | Skipped because platform or tooling is unavailable; state why and do not pretend completion. |

### 0.3 Task status table

Rebuild or update this table at every startup. Do not treat "docs say done" as done; code, tests, and gates are authoritative.

Fully closed rows may have their detailed evidence moved out of this prompt
into `docs/current-goal-state.md` or a routed archive/evidence document, but the
task board keeps one compact status row plus the claim boundary and authority
links. `DONE_WEAK` rows stay visible until their open boundary is closed.

becoming mark roots. The pcc-Python runtime mirror adds
`_py_obj_visit_weakref_slots(...)` with the same role split for trace,
cycle-ref subtraction, promotion, backend-4 remap, and owned-only clear, and
the backend0 cycle-collector port adds `_py_obj_gc_visit_weakref_slots(...)`.

Previous AUD-P0-GC-SLOT-VISITOR supplement (2026-07-03): trace/subtract slot
consumers now read through the relocation load barrier. C
`pcc_gc_trace_owner_slot(...)` no longer calls the trace visitor on raw `*slot`;

cycle-reference subtraction observe the same forwarding/read-barrier view as
the C runtime slot contract. Update and clear modes remain separate: remap

Task-board correction note (2026-07-04): for `AUD-P0-GC-SLOT-VISITOR`,
weakref is no longer described as part of the generic fixed-owner helper.
Current source truth is a dedicated weakref helper: `target` is borrowed
update-only and `callback` is owned in C, pcc-Python `py_gc_backend.py`, and
backend0 `py_obj_gc.py`. The row remains `DONE_WEAK`; this latest slice moves
one more family into the contract but does not close broader value payload
slots or remaining pcc-Python mirror parity. Latest payload-span correction:
backend-4 owner payload spans are additive per owner, and relocated
`PY_TYPE_CLASS` `bases`/`mro`/`methods` arrays now register spans in C and the
pcc-Python runtime mirror so external class metadata slots get correct zpage
card mapping. Latest class-creation correction: initial `py_class_new`
`bases`/`mro` arrays and growing `py_class_add_method` method tables are also
registered on both C and pcc-Python sides; method-table `realloc` uses the
payload-span retarget API instead of losing the original virtual zpage offset.
Latest C-extension object correction: dynamic pcc-native C-extension type tags
now route through `pcc_capi_visit_cext_object_slots` / `tp_traverse` /
fake-header `Py_VISIT` before the generic instance walker, and backend-4
relocation-copy explicitly rejects opaque C-extension objects instead of
treating `PCC_CAPI_CEXT_TAG_BASE+N` as a pcc user-instance layout.
Latest dynamic-tag deferral correction: dynamic pcc-native C-extension tags now
short-circuit C `pcc_trash_should_defer(...)`, split C
`pcc_dealloc_should_defer(...)`, and pcc-Python `_dealloc_should_defer(...)`
before the generic user-tag deferral fallback; the split C helper also has
explicit `return 1` for the concrete pointer-bearing families.
Latest backend0 mirror correction: pcc-Python `py_obj_gc.py`
`_py_obj_gc_visit_instance_owner_slots(...)` now excludes dynamic
C-extension tags before its instance/valuebox/user-class fallback, matching the
C and generic pcc-Python backend slot-dispatch boundary.

### 0.6 Mandatory status-update rules

Codex must update the status board at these points:

1. **Before starting**: fill in `run_id`, commit, branch, scan documents, and update the task status table.
2. **After selecting a task**: fill in the selected-task card and change the selected task status to `IN_PROGRESS`.
3. **After writing tests**: record the test name and expected failure reason; if the test cannot fail, explain why.
4. **After implementation**: record which mechanisms changed; do not only write "fixed issue".
5. **After testing**: record the exact command, pass/fail, and failure summary; do not fabricate test results. If the slice touches pcc1, self-backend, no-libpython, runtime/GC/rooting/object lifetime, shared Python lowering, valueclass/valuebox behavior, or a value-payload GC contract, record the required `bootstrap: passed|failed|not run` line from §0.9 immediately with the rest of the validation state.
6. **When blocked**: change status to `BLOCKED`, and write the blocker, minimal repro, ruled-out causes, and next step.
7. **Before completion**: mark `DONE_STRONG` only when completion conditions are met; otherwise mark `DONE_WEAK` or `TODO_NEEDS_DESIGN`. For the surfaces named in §0.9, do not mark `DONE_WEAK` or `DONE_STRONG` while the bootstrap line is missing.

### 0.7 `DONE_STRONG` completion conditions

A task may be marked `DONE_STRONG` only when all of these are true:

- The implementation is generic, not a hard-coded special case.
- A focused regression test exists.
- A negative or boundary test prevents wrong optimization or silent wrong behavior.
- If the claim involves pcc1, there is `PCC_HOST_PYTHON=/bin/false` or equivalent no-host evidence.
- If the claim involves no-libpython, there is a linkage scan or explicit no-libpython evidence.
- If the claim involves runtime/GC/rooting/object lifetime or any shared
  lowering that can change bootstrap object ownership, full-bootstrap evidence
  must be all-five-GC evidence: the pcc0->pcc1->pcc2->pcc3 gate must be proven
  under `PCC_GC_BACKEND=0..4` or through the dedicated all-five bootstrap
  matrix once implemented. Backend #0-only bootstrap is not a strong runtime/GC
  completion claim.
- If the claim involves performance, there is an IR-shape gate and runtime benchmark.
- If the claim involves package/C-extension behavior, there is ABI mode, manifest, and error-path evidence.
- If the claim involves self-backend, there is self-involvement/no-fallback evidence.
- Docs/status board are updated and explicitly state what was proved and not proved.

### 0.8 `BLOCKED` handling protocol

When blocked, do not keep blindly editing. Output and record:

```text
blocked_task_id: <ID>
blocker_kind: semantic | codegen | runtime | self-backend | pcc1-no-host | test-design | perf | package | unknown
minimal_repro: <path or code snippet>
last_good_step: <most recent passing step>
observed_failure: <stderr/stdout/exception summary>
known_not_causes: <causes already ruled out>
next_probe: <next minimal probe>
```

### 0.9 Evidence format

All evidence must be reproducible. Commands must be written in full, for example:

```bash
env -u LC_ALL uv run pytest tests/python/test_x.py::test_y -q -n0
PCC_HOST_PYTHON=/bin/false build/bootstrap-pytest-self/pcc1 -m pcc.package ext-abi --json
otool -L build/bootstrap-pytest-self/pcc1
```

If a test was not run, write `not run` and explain why. Do not write "should pass".

Any completion or validation summary for a slice that touches pcc1,
self-backend, no-libpython, runtime/GC/rooting/object lifetime, shared Python
lowering, valueclass/valuebox behavior, or a value-payload GC contract must
include an explicit bootstrap line. The line must say one of:

```text
bootstrap: passed (<exact gate and result>)
bootstrap: failed (<first failing boundary and result>)
bootstrap: not run (<why this slice does not require it, or why the claim is not complete>)
```

Omitting the bootstrap line is itself a validation gap. A focused unit-test,
GC-contract, `py_compile`, or `git diff --check` list without the required
bootstrap status is not a completed claim for those surfaces.

### 0.10 Claim hygiene

Every claim in the status board must map to a gate:

```text
host pcc pass          != pcc1 pass
cpython-compat pass    != pcc-native pass
libpython mode pass    != no-libpython pass
fake package pass      != real package pass
array-core pass        != import numpy pass
stage1 self-backed     != pcc1->pcc2->pcc3 self-backed
metadata exists        != runtime implementation complete
microbenchmark win     != whole-program performance win
```

### 0.11 Runtime-effect / resource-contract claim hygiene

Runtime-effect work is a verification and routing layer over the existing PCC
runtime ABI. It must not be described as a new GC, scheduler, GPU backend, or
runtime replacement unless the touched implementation path and gates prove that
claim.

Every runtime-effect claim must say which level is proven:

```text
taxonomy only                  != compiler checker
compiler checker               != runtime behavior change
host-pcc checker pass          != pcc1 no-host checker pass
single GC backend pass         != all-five-GC runtime/rooting contract
barrier classification exists  != all slot writes are barrier-safe
root bracket checker exists    != all generated exits/suspensions are proven
GPU host/device resource model != real device memory runtime
Metal artifact exists          != MLX/native tensor runtime support
virtual-thread substrate       != arbitrary Loom-style stack copying
```

Runtime-effect tasks must preserve these boundaries:

1. Do not bypass `pcc_gc_load_ptr`, `pcc_gc_store_ptr`, `pcc_gc_store_root`,
   frame-root registration, continuation-root registration, safepoints, or pin

4. If a runtime-effect slice touches `pcc/py_runtime/`, shared Python lowering,

## 0. Your role

You are the long-term engineering agent for this repo, not a one-shot patch generator.

Your task is not "write a patch that looks testable". Your task is to continuously advance pcc toward its end state:

```text
pcc1 can replace python.
pcc can compile Python into no-libpython native artifacts.
pcc preserves CPython semantics where supported.
pcc fails loudly where strict native mode cannot prove semantics yet.
pcc achieves C-like speed on statically provable hot paths.
pcc makes package / extension / stdlib / runtime / GC / self-backend claims honest and reproducible.
```

Do not avoid hard work. The goal is to climb the mountain, not to build a demo toy.

Do not deceive yourself either. Weak tests, fake implementations, hard-coded special cases, weaker assertions, and overclaims must not be used to manufacture "completion".

---

## 1. North star and engineering boundaries

### 1.1 Overall goal

The long-term goal of pcc is:

> To become a no-libpython CPython-compatible native runtime and compiler, able to replace Python with pcc1 for key workflows and approach C-like performance on hot paths with proven semantics.

This is neither a conservative goal nor a short-term demo goal.

### 1.2 The two slogans must appear together

```text
Write Python. Run Native.
C-like speed where Python semantics can be proven.
Exact Python semantics everywhere supported.
```

The first sentence gives product direction. The second gives engineering boundaries. Any document that keeps only the first and deletes the second may overclaim.

### 1.3 Source compatibility and binary ABI compatibility must stay separate

```text
source compatibility
  -> User `.py`, stdlib, package, import, exception, descriptor, metaclass, async, GC, weakref, and threading behavior run with CPython semantics.

pcc-native extension ABI
  -> Native C extension ABI targeting the pcc runtime, without depending on libpython.

CPython C-API compatibility
  -> Gradually implement public C-API surface such as PyModuleDef, PyMethodDef, capsule, buffer, dict/list/tuple/unicode/int helpers.

CPython binary ABI compatibility
  -> Arbitrary `.so`/`.pyd` assumes CPython object layout, PyObject_HEAD, GIL, and private APIs. This must be an explicit compat mode, not misrepresented as pcc-native.
```

Replacing CPython must climb this gradient:

```text
source compatibility
→ pcc-native extension ABI
→ CPython public C-API compatibility
→ CPython binary ABI compatibility as explicit mode
```

Do not present a `cpython-compat` or `libpython` path as completed `pcc-native no-libpython` support.

## R-P1: runtime-effect category / resource contract

This track makes PCC runtime composition explicit without replacing the existing
runtime ABI. It is a checker/protocol track first.

### Current problem

PCC already has GC roots, frame maps, load/store barriers, continuation roots,
scheduler queues, virtual-thread suspension points, and GPU host/device split
surfaces. They are implemented across `pcc/py_runtime/`,
`pcc/py_frontend/codegen/`, and GPU lowering files, but the compiler does not
yet have one small resource/effect contract that says which operations allocate,
retain, release, read-barrier, write-barrier, root, unroot, pin, suspend,
resume, enqueue, dequeue, transfer, launch, or sync.

Without this contract, future GC/scheduler/GPU changes can pass focused tests
while still weakening composition boundaries.

### Goal

Add a small, self-host-safe runtime-effect/resource taxonomy and checker path
that can classify existing runtime ABI calls and later verify selected generated
IR/codegen event paths.

The first slice is taxonomy + tests only. It must not change runtime behavior.

### First implementation slice

Add:

```text
pcc/category.py
pcc/runtime_effects.py
tests/python/test_category_kernel.py
tests/python/test_runtime_effect_category.py
docs/plans/runtime-effect-category-plan.md
```

The first checker must classify at least:

```text
pcc_gc_alloc
pcc_gc_retain
pcc_gc_release
pcc_gc_load_ptr
pcc_gc_load_borrowed_ptr
pcc_gc_store_ptr
pcc_gc_store_root
pcc_gc_frame_enter
pcc_gc_frame_leave
pcc_gc_safepoint
pcc_gc_collect
pcc_gc_pin
pcc_gc_unpin
pcc_gc_register_continuation_root
pcc_gc_unregister_continuation_root
pcc_gc_scheduler_queue_push
pcc_gc_scheduler_queue_pop_into
py_continuation_new_typed
py_virtual_thread_start
py_virtual_thread_park
py_virtual_thread_unpark
py_virtual_thread_sleep
py_virtual_thread_block_on_fd
py_virtual_thread_run_once
py_virtual_thread_run_until_idle
```

### Non-goals for the first slice

- Do not modify `pcc/py_runtime/src/*.c`.
- Do not modify `pcc/py_runtime/py/*.py`.
- Do not change generated IR.
- Do not claim new GC, scheduler, virtual-thread, or GPU runtime behavior.
- Do not require all `pcc_gc_backend4_*` telemetry functions to be classified in
  the first slice; classify correctness-critical ABI first.

### Acceptance

Focused gate:

```bash
env -u LC_ALL uv run pytest tests/python/test_category_kernel.py tests/python/test_runtime_effect_category.py -q -n0
```

If the slice only adds taxonomy/checker tests and does not affect codegen/runtime:

```text
bootstrap: not run (taxonomy/checker-only; no codegen/runtime behavior change)
gc_matrix: not touched
claim_boundary: checker taxonomy only; no runtime behavior change
```

## P0: self-host-safe structured codegen diagnostics

Current failure mode:
stage2-produced compiler can lose traceback/message on codegen failures.
The outer failure becomes an empty PyPipelineError, so debugging requires
manual breadcrumbs. We need a small self-host-safe diagnostic rail.

Goal:
Enhance existing PCC_DEBUG_CODEGEN_PHASES, without adding a new module, so that
pcc2/pcc3 can print the last codegen breadcrumbs even when Python traceback or
exception message is lost.

Implement three minimal capabilities:

1. phase breadcrumb
   - record module, function, stmt_index, stmt_kind, expr_kind, and span when safe
   - keep a fixed-size last-N ring buffer
   - do not use f-string, generator expression, complex repr, or dynamic formatting
     in the diagnostic path

2. boundary catch
   - at stmt/expr/function/module codegen boundaries, catch BaseException
   - record exception type and current AST node kind/span
   - print breadcrumb dump to stderr when PCC_DEBUG_CODEGEN_PHASES is enabled
   - re-raise the original exception; do not swallow or wrap locally

3. stage-safe formatter
   - pcc2/pcc3 must be able to print the last N breadcrumbs even if Python
     traceback/message is unavailable
   - prefer fixed strings, integer codes, simple str(int), simple string concat
   - JSON/profile output is optional after stderr works; do not expand self-host
     surface just to write JSON

Tests:
- focused failing-codegen test asserts stderr contains PCC_CODEGEN_EXCEPTION
  and PCC_CODEGEN_BREADCRUMB
- expr-boundary failure includes expr kind
- stmt-boundary failure includes stmt index/kind
- debug flag disabled means no breadcrumb spam
- if pcc1 exists, run a PCC_HOST_PYTHON=/bin/false pcc1 no-host variant

Non-goals:
- do not implement a large new diagnostics framework
- do not add a new module yet
- do not rely on repr(AST), f-string, join(generator), getattr default, or
  complex JSON formatting in the diagnostic path
- do not mask the underlying exception

Acceptance:
- The current _parse_float_literal_lift failure can be localized to a concrete
  module/function/stmt_index/expr_kind/span.
- The failure output remains useful even when PyPipelineError has an empty
  message.
- Normal codegen output is unchanged when PCC_DEBUG_CODEGEN_PHASES is off.


## P0: pcc1 self-host Python parity blockers

These are not optional ergonomics. They are required for pcc1 to replace Python.
Temporary rewrites may be used only to isolate a failure, but every rewrite must
leave behind a focused regression test and a real fix task.

### Policy

- Do not permanently avoid Python features that pcc1 should support.
- Do not replace generator expressions, f-strings, string concat, getattr
  default, or short-circuit expressions merely to pass bootstrap.
- If a temporary workaround is used to isolate a separate bug, add a TODO and a
  regression test for the original Python construct.
- All fixes must run through pcc1/no-host where possible:
  `PCC_HOST_PYTHON=/bin/false`.
- Every feature below needs:
  1. CPython differential or expected-output test.
  2. pcc native compile/run test.
  3. pcc1 self-host/no-host test where applicable.
  4. Negative/boundary test if semantics can be mislowered.

### Coverage Ratchet (pcc1 + pcc2)

- If pcc1/pcc2 semantic coverage is incomplete for a touched feature, do not
  close the work as "done".
- Add or extend focused tests for both pcc1 and pcc2 paths (not only host pcc)
  before considering the fix complete.
- If a blocker prevents immediate full coverage, record the exact missing cases
  and follow-up test tasks in `codex-goal-prompt.md` and the active
  investigation doc in the same change.
- Prefer small, isolated parity tests that pin one Python semantic each, then
  keep a running checklist of uncovered semantics until all are ratcheted in.
- No regression fix is complete if it only passes bootstrap by rewrite while
  leaving the original construct untested in pcc1/pcc2.

### If pcc1 and pcc2 differ

Classify the difference before fixing:

1. semantic execution difference
2. codegen IR difference
3. class field layout difference
4. backend selection difference
5. object/link metadata difference
6. runtime archive/linkage difference
7. diagnostic/error-path difference
8. performance-only difference
9. unknown

Do not patch around the symptom until the difference class is known.


### Required Parity Cases (Current P0 Checklist)

The following semantics must have explicit pcc1 + pcc2 parity coverage. If any
item is still flaky or unsupported, keep it open as a tracked blocker.

1. Generator expressions, including constructor/call argument positions:
   `", ".join(f"{a.type} {a}" for a in args_list)` and `tuple(genexpr)`.
2. self-host `try` lowering stability, including `try/except` value flow.
3. `getattr(obj, "name", default)` default-value semantics.
4. Truthiness and branch semantics for `if args or kwargs`.
5. Runtime string concatenation behavior under self-host (`a + b` paths).
6. Short-circuit lowering correctness (`and` / `or`) without mislower.
7. f-string runtime formatting path stability (`py_obj_format`) in self-host.
8. IR text/string assembly paths that format LLVM Type/Value objects (no fragile
   f-string/object-probing behavior at compile time).
9. `_should_box_python_ints()` consistency across pcc1/pcc2/self-host paths.
10. Constructor-arg boundary fallback for simple literals (`int`/`str`/`bool`/`None`)
    when normal expression emission returns invalid/null values.
11. Literal dispatch must not rely only on `ty.name == "str"`; AST-literal-kind
    dispatch is required, with `ty.name` only as fallback.
12. Cross-module self-host boundaries where AST class identity and `ty.name`
    can drift must be covered with parity tests.
13. Metadata access edges such as `init_fn_args[i].type` returning null on
    tuple/foreign-object boundaries must have tolerant handling and tests.
14. Slice + assign/call boundaries used in bootstrap paths (e.g. `argv[1:]`)
    must be validated in pcc1+pcc2.
15. Empty-decorator / empty-sequence iteration boundaries in self-host lowering
    (no crash/miscompile on zero-length paths).
16. Missing/optional span metadata (`expr.span` absent) must not crash codegen;
    diagnostics should degrade gracefully.

For each checklist item, include:
- CPython differential (or expected output) test.
- host pcc compile/run test.
- pcc1 self-host/no-host test.
- pcc2 test.
- negative/boundary variant when mislower risk exists.

## 2. Document routing and reference discipline

Do not bulk-read every related plan, issue, investigation, or historical
ledger before choosing a slice. The startup set is intentionally small:

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `codex-goal-prompt.md`
3. `docs/current-goal-state.md`

`docs/current-goal-state.md` owns the on-demand reference router. Open
additional documents only when the selected task, a failing gate, or a claim
boundary crosses into the routed branch.

### 2.1 Default startup contract

- `AGENTS.md` owns repository operating rules and validation discipline.
- `codex-goal-prompt.md` owns the long-form objective, priority model,
  parity policy, coverage ratchet, gates, claim hygiene, and output contract.
- `docs/current-goal-state.md` owns the short audit, latest evidence,
  weak-boundary list, claim-authority map, and branch-specific reference
  routes.

### 2.2 On-demand branch references

Branch docs are pointers, not startup requirements. Use the routing tables in
`docs/current-goal-state.md` for:

- self-backend bootstrap/defaulting plans
- self-backend translation plans
- Python frontend/runtime/fallback plans
- performance plans
- value-model plans
- GC and virtual-thread references
- NumPy/package/ecosystem plans
- investigation indexes

Do not copy branch-plan bodies into this prompt. If a route changes, update
the router in `docs/current-goal-state.md` unless the reference is a global
protocol authority.

### 2.3 Evidence authorities

Current focused tests, bootstrap gates, and JSON baselines outrank prose. Use
the completion-claim authority table in `docs/current-goal-state.md` before
promoting a slice beyond focused evidence.

## 3. Global working principles

1. Skip work that is already implemented and proven by strong gates; do not rebuild it.
2. For planned but unimplemented work, first organize the task list, then pick the most critical minimal closed loop.
3. Implementation must be elegant, generic, and maintainable; test-specific special cases are forbidden.
4. Tests must be complete enough to catch real semantics and failure modes; shallow tests are not acceptable.
5. Every change needs diagnostics, negative tests, and awareness of pcc1/no-host paths.
6. `pcc1 can replace python` is the end goal; do not stop at host pcc.
7. The five GC backends, self-backend, Valhalla/value model, virtual threads, package/C-API, stdlib, and performance specialization must work together.
8. Every broad claim must have a reproducible gate.
9. Unsupported dynamic semantics must fail loudly, not silently behave incorrectly.
10. Performance claims must include both IR-shape evidence and runtime benchmarks.

---

## 4. Repository execution discipline

This prompt must independently guide an agent working in the `pcc` repo. Before any implementation, follow these execution rules.

### 4.1 Commands and environment

```text
- Use `env -u LC_ALL uv run ...` for Python entrypoints.
- Prefer `-n0` when debugging one failure, so xdist does not hide ordering or temp-file problems.
- Use `rg` / `rg --files` for search.
- Run probe binaries with a hard timeout.
- Before finishing, check for leftover probe / pytest / pcc1 processes.
```

Recommended probe wrapper:

```bash
timeout 30s /tmp/pcc_probe
pgrep -af '([p]ccnpapi|[p]cc1_probe|[p]q_probe_stage|[m]ain_bin|[p]ytest|[u]v run|scripts/[b]ootstrap|build/[b]ootstrap-pytest-self/pcc1)'
```

### 4.2 Worktree safety

```text
- The worktree may already contain dirty changes by other people; inspect first, do not overwrite.
- Do not run `git reset --hard` / `git checkout --` / `git restore` / `git clean` / `git stash` / destructive branch switches.
- Do not `git commit` unless the user explicitly asks or the green-gate local
  commit workflow above applies. Never push from that workflow.
- Do not force-add ignored files. `git add -f <ignored-path>` requires an
  explicit user instruction naming that ignored path.
- Do not put scratch `.c` / `.py` / generated artifacts in the repo root.
- For temporary probes, prefer a real regression test, then an existing cache/build directory, and only then `/tmp`.
- Use patch-style edits for manual file edits; do not overwrite shared files with shell heredocs.
```

If you see unrelated dirty files:

```text
1. Do not revert them.
2. Do not format unrelated files.
3. Do not mix unrelated diffs into this turn summary.
4. If the same file already has changes from someone else, read the context and edit only the minimal region.
```

### 4.3 Diagnosis and investigation discipline

Minimize any non-trivial bug first:

```text
integration failure
→ focused pytest node / CLI repro
→ minimized C or Python program
→ semantic or IR-level reproducer
```

When touching `pcc/codegen/c_codegen.py`, `pcc/py_frontend/codegen/layer1.py`, `native_*.py`, runtime GC, or self-backend:

```text
- Add the smallest regression first.
- Run the focused gate after every shared-path edit.
- Do not stack multiple unverified guesses.
- If the first fix does not improve the minimal repro, return to reduction instead of expanding the patch.
```

Bootstrap regression causality audit is mandatory before patching:

```text
- If a full bootstrap or pcc1 smoke gate has been green for a long time, treat
  the current worktree's recent edits as the primary suspect until evidence
  rules them out.
- Identify the first failing boundary: host-side test, pcc0->pcc1 compile,
  pcc1 smoke compile, pcc1->pcc2 compile/run, pcc2->pcc3 compare, fallback
  baseline, or all-five-GC runtime gate.
- List the recent touched subsystems that can plausibly own that boundary,
  including frontend/codegen ownership, return conventions, runtime/GC roots,
  backend emission, and bootstrap CLI changes.
- Separate stacked failures. Fix and re-run the first boundary before treating
  later traces as root cause.
- Do not bypass a bootstrap regression by weakening GC/runtime semantics,
  disabling tracking, dropping barriers, skipping releases, recapturing a
  baseline, or loosening strict no-libpython mode.
- For ownership/lifetime failures, audit the caller/callee ownership contract
  first. A fix must preserve the generic runtime contract, not only the latest
  bootstrap trace.
- Investigation reports are required evidence, not substitutes for the
  causality audit, regression test, and gate rerun.
```

When written investigation is needed:

```text
- Check `docs/investigations/INDEX.md` first.
- If a prior investigation exists, append `## Update`; do not delete history.
- Write new investigations to `docs/investigations/<specific-topic>.md`.
- After updating investigations, run `env -u LC_ALL uv run python scripts/regen_investigations_index.py`.
```

```text
Darwin arm64 supported-host default

```

### V-track：Valhalla / value model

Goal: opt-in identity-free value payloads provide a real performance breakthrough for Python hot paths.

Scope:

```text
@pcc.valueclass
ValueClassType
ValuePayload
ValueBox
constructor payload ABI
field extract/insert
method receiver payload ABI
fieldwise equality/hash
boxing/unboxing boundary
identity escape diagnostics
flattened fields
value arrays / typed containers
GC tracing of pointer-bearing payloads
generic specialization
```

#### Projection model: borrow Valhalla's projection, NOT Java `int`'s wrap

The value model's core idea (distilled from Project Valhalla) is **separation of
semantic type from physical representation**: identity is a semantic cost; a
value with no observable identity may be given a freer physical representation;
the object/ref boundary is managed by an explicit projection / boxing bridge;
ordinary semantics are never silently changed; performance comes from a legal
representation, not from a changed language semantics. What pcc borrows is the
*projection model*. What pcc does NOT borrow is Java's fixed-width `int`
overflow/wrap semantics.

Every semantic type has (potentially) two projections:

```text
Python `int`  (semantic type = arbitrary precision, ALWAYS)
  ├── value projection : tagged small-int inline fast lane (i63-ish)
  └── object projection: PyInt / boxed bignum
      -> overflow of the value projection DEOPTs/PROMOTEs to the object
         projection. It MUST NOT wrap. semantics == CPython.

pcc.i64 / pcc.u64  (explicit machine-integer semantic type)
  └── raw i64/u64 projection, machine semantics.
      The overflow policy (wrap / trap / checked / saturating) is part of the
      type and must be written explicitly. THIS is where Java/C-style fixed
      width lives — never under plain `int`.

@pcc.valueclass C  (user value payload)
  ├── value projection : LLVM aggregate payload
  └── object projection: ValueBox / PyObject boundary
      Field semantics follow the field's TYPE: an `int` field is Python
      arbitrary-precision (optimized via the tagged lane); a `pcc.i64` field is
      raw machine. The field type, not the valueclass-ness, decides.
```

Acknowledge the seam (JEP 402 keeps a primitive/reference seam; pcc keeps a
value/object seam): do NOT pretend `Python int == i64` or that boxed and
unboxed ints are indistinguishable. A `Python int` value may be inlined in some
places and boxed in others; the boundary is explicit and overflow deopts/
promotes. The current typed-int implementation (IntType -> `_to_int64` -> raw
`builder.add/sub/mul`) is exactly the confusion this model forbids — it equates
the Python semantic type with the machine representation and so wraps. The fix
(see docs/investigations/typed-int-unboxed-overflow-silent-wraparound.md) is to
implement `int`'s value/object projection honestly: tagged fast lane + boxed
bignum promotion; reserve raw i64 for `pcc.i64` or a provably-in-range
sub-expression. `int` is Python bigint; raw i64 is an explicit machine type or a
proven-safe internal optimization, never the default meaning of `int`.

### G-track: five GC backends

Goal: each of the five GC backends reaches its own peak without dragging down the main line.

Suggested roles:

```text
backend #0: correctness/reference/default rollback path
backend #1: incremental pause/debt model
backend #2: concurrent mark/sweep, worker/assist/STW/threaded path
backend #3: generational allocation performance challenger
backend #4: relocating/update/read-barrier/high-end research path
```

The roles above are **performance / algorithmic-policy** roles only. They do NOT
imply a semantic hierarchy: see the 5-GC Production Equality Rule below — all
five backends owe the SAME Python semantic contract. "challenger" / "research
path" describes a backend's perf maturity, not a second-class semantic status.

### 5-GC Production Equality Rule (sharpens obligation 6)

pcc has five GC backends. All five are production targets.

Backend #0 may be the default selection (compatibility / rollout / rollback
reference), but it is NOT the only production backend and must not receive
privileged Python semantics. `#0 default != #0 only-production`;
`#1/#2/#3/#4 selectable != experimental`.

A runtime feature is not production-complete until the same feature passes the
common GC production contract under:

- `PCC_GC_BACKEND=0` — refcount + cycle collector
- `PCC_GC_BACKEND=1` — incremental tricolor mark-sweep
- `PCC_GC_BACKEND=2` — concurrent mark-sweep
- `PCC_GC_BACKEND=3` — generational young/old
- `PCC_GC_BACKEND=4` — relocating / ZGC-style backend

**Production equality means (semantics — hard requirement, may NOT differ):**
same object reachability; root safety; exception/frame survival; container
graph safety; weakref/finalizer/resurrection safety policy; extension object
lifetime safety; ValueBox/value-payload pointer safety; virtual-thread
suspended-frame and scheduler-root safety; no-libpython pcc1 behavior where the
feature is claimed.

**Production equality does NOT require (perf — reportable, MAY differ):**
identical pause times, throughput, RSS, fragmentation profile, or collection
schedule. Performance is a backend-specific profile; semantics is not.

**Status rule (status vocabulary §0.2):** a runtime feature touching objects,
references, lifetime, GC roots, exceptions, frames, containers, extensions,
ValueBox, or virtual threads is `DONE_STRONG` only if it passes all five
backends:

```bash
for b in 0 1 2 3 4; do
  PCC_GC_BACKEND=$b env -u LC_ALL uv run pytest <focused-feature-tests> -q -n0
done
```

Passes only #0 -> `DONE_WEAK`. Passes some-but-not-all -> `BACKEND_PARTIAL`
(new status; not production-complete). Any skipped backend -> the skip reason
must be explicit; the feature may NOT be called production-complete /
production-ready / pcc-native complete. Backend-specific algorithm suites are
ADDITIONAL, never substitutes for the common contract. Any production backend
failing the common contract is a release blocker (emergency rollback must
mode-label "backend #N temporarily disabled / not production this release").

**Full bootstrap rule:** the target full-bootstrap gate for runtime/GC,
rooting, object-lifetime, and shared Python-lowering work is an all-five-GC
matrix: the same source must pass strict pcc0->pcc1->pcc2->pcc3 bootstrap under
`PCC_GC_BACKEND=0`, `1`, `2`, `3`, and `4`, with the normal pcc2/pcc3 compare
for each backend. Until the pytest gate is implemented as that matrix, agents
must report single-backend bootstrap as partial evidence only for runtime/GC
claims and must pair it with the current common production contract.

**Engineering mechanism (so 5-GC equality is not 5x hand-maintenance):**
every runtime object type declares its reference slots ONCE via a slot-based
trace/update contract (strong / weak / borrowed / pinned / movable /
native-handle / value-payload-pointer / frame-local / scheduler-root, plus
non-traced scalar payloads + finalizer/resurrection behavior); all five
backends consume the same `py_obj_visit_slots(obj, visitor)` contract (#0
reachability/cycle, #1 mark barrier, #2 work-buffer, #3 remembered-set/
promotion, #4 forwarding/slot-update). GC backends must NOT hand-code
per-type object-graph walkers (`if object is list / valuebox / coroutine ...`).
New runtime objects (PyValueBox, CoroutineFrame, VirtualThread, Task,
MemoryView, ExtensionModuleState, NativeHandle, TypedArray, ValueArray, ...)
file a GC Object Contract Checklist (slot contract + 5 backend gates + C/
pcc-Python mirror parity + pcc1 no-host) before merge. C runtime and
pcc-Python mirror must pass mirror parity under all five backends
(2 impls x 5 backends) before production-complete. A common contract suite
lives at `tests/python/gc_production_contract/` with runner
`scripts/run_gc_production_contract.sh` (all-five-green = "5-GC production
contract pass").

> Status of this rule (2026-05-31): ADOPTED as the principle. The mechanism
> (slot contract, common suite, mirror x5 runner, per-object checklists) is a
> large engineering PROGRAM, not yet built — tracked here as the G-track
> production bar. Existing docs that frame #1–#4 as "challenger / advanced /
> experimental" describe perf maturity and must be read through this rule
> (semantic equality required; perf profile may vary). See
> `docs/investigations/gc-backend-selection-matrix.md` for the current default
> selection (#0) and per-backend perf/algorithm status.

### T-track：virtual thread / scheduler roots

Goal: virtual threads first solve GC root/update correctness, then higher-level scheduling performance.

Scope:

```text
stackless coroutine/task heap frame
suspended frame roots
scheduler queues as GC roots

safepoint metadata

IO/timer ready queue
```
